newsitem.title: UK: UK gives secret asylum to China dissidents -report.
newsitem.headline: UK gives secret asylum to China dissidents -report.

text.p: Britain has secretly granted political asylum to five Chinese dissidents recently based in Hong Kong, said the Independent on Sunday newspaper.
One was a student leader of the 1989 pro-democracy movement.

"The five -- three men and two women, all thought to be in their late 20s -- were involved in the pro-democracy movement which culminated in the Tiananmen Square massacre," the paper said. "They have been granted full political asylum in Britain with rights to social benefis, the immediate right to work and the right to a British passport after four years."

The paper quoted one of the unidentified dissidents as saying the move was arranged in cooperation with the Hong Kong government, British officials and human rights groups. The dissident was now living in Britain under a new name, it said.
British officials said they could not discuss the case.

"Details of the arrival of the seven people -- two are dependants -- have been kept confidential in an attempt to avoid upsetting the Chinese authorities in the run-up to the Hong Kong handover a week tomorrow," the weekly paper said.
"This is the first confirmation of Britain specifically helping anti-Peking political activists."

While the United States, Holland and Finland, among others, have granted asylum to those fearing for their safety as Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule, Britain has been criticised for not doing more to help the dissidents.
